title: Era-specific annual phases raise a fixed Gl 229 mismatch scale from 2.09 to 7.78 m/s in a 60-visit design
abstract: We test a future observing plan for the reported 122-day Gl 229 signal and a 121.75-day annual harmonic. We use 197 public historical nights and 60 trial dates in 2027 to 2031. With fixed periods and independent 1 m/s errors, a greedy plan needs a worst-phase amplitude of 2.09 m/s to give a squared noise-scaled mismatch of 25 if the annual amplitude and phase are shared across all dates. The scale rises to 7.78 m/s if the annual response can change in three instrument eras. A uniform plan gives 1.9 and 8.0 m/s. Allowing only the future annual response to change gives 6.75 m/s. These are exact design values, not observed detection limits or five-sigma thresholds. We find no new planet or physical signal. Noise correlations, free periods, instrument physics and telescope constraints are not tested. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, synthetic schedules and exact external input provenance are included. External source records are not bundled.

display.caption: Fixed-period design comparison under independent 1 m/s errors. Left: amplitude for a worst-phase squared noise-scaled mismatch of 25. This is not a significance threshold. Right: minimum residual energy in 200 random schedules; dashed lines show the greedy plan. Annual phase per era also allows a separate amplitude.

citations.reason: Historical sampling ambiguity and fixed annual-harmonic control motivate this new future-design test. We use the same external source, not earlier code.
